source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting a failed industrial safety audit

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Collect all inspection records related to the audit. This will include the inspection checklist, observations made by the auditor, and any notes or photographs taken during the inspection. Ensure that all relevant documentation is organized and filed, as it will provide the core evidence of the audit findings.

2. Write a summary report.
Prepare a comprehensive summary report that outlines the areas where the facility failed to meet safety standards. Clearly list each standard that was not met, providing concise descriptions of how and where the failure occurred. Use specific examples and observations to support your findings.

3. Identify deviations from standards.
Detail each deviation from required safety standards. Provide the relevant regulation or guideline and describe how the facility fell short. Categorize the deviations according to their severity, from minor infractions to major violations that pose immediate safety risks.

4. Document contributing factors.
Identify and document any contributing factors that led to the failed audit. This could include lack of training, outdated equipment, insufficient
